title: Protocol to assess two distinct components of the nonlinear capacitance in mouse cardiomyocytes
protocol: Preheat the water bath to 37°C.
Inject mice with 80 mg/kg ketamine and 5 mg/kg xylazine intraperitoneally.
Assess level of anesthesia by firm toe pinch.
Inject 300 USP unit sodium heparin intraperitoneally.
Perform a midline thoracotomy and heart excision.
Transfer the heart to a petri dish containing ice-cold Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution.
Trim the connective tissues using a fine scissor.
Cannulate the heart through aorta onto a Langendorff apparatus prefilled with Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution, gassed with 100% O2.
Retrogradely perfuse the heart with the Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution at 37°C using a perfusion pump.
Washout blood by perfusing for 3 minutes.
Adjust the perfusion speed to a flow rate of 4–6 mL/min and control initial pressure at ≈75 mmHg using a pressure monitor connected to the Langendorff apparatus.
Switch the perfusion solution to Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution containing collagenase type II (0.8 mg/mL) for tissue digestion.
Monitor the perfusion pressure during tissue digestion by collagenase type II for 15–20 minutes until it falls below 30 mmHg.
Check the color of the heart surface and assess the softness of the heart tissue to determine the digestion level.
Perfuse the heart with high potassium solution for 3 minutes.
Remove the heart from the perfusion apparatus and transfer it to a petri dish containing high potassium solution.
Mince the left ventricle and mechanically dissociate the tissue by pipetting.
Harvest single isolated cardiomyocytes by filtering through a nylon mesh cell strainer (100 μm).
Store the cardiomyocytes in high potassium solution at room temperature for recording.
Prepare glass patch pipettes from borosilicate glass capillaries using a P-97 micropipette puller.
Polish the pipette tips with a microforge to achieve an electrode resistance of 1.5–3.0 MΩ when filled with the pipette solution.
Fill pipettes with a small amount of internal solution to minimize capacitance.
Use relatively thicker wall glass capillaries for pipettes.
Coat the pipette tip with SYLARDTM 184 to reduce capacitance.
Set the voltage-clamp protocol in Clampex 10 software.
Set the stair voltage protocol ranging from −140 to +100 mV with a 10-mV increment.
Seed cardiomyocytes in a recording chamber with a volume size of 0.5 mL connected to a gravity driven solution perfusion system.
Keep the perfusion speed at 1–2 mL/min.
Maintain the solution level low to minimize pipette capacitance and reduce the depth of the pipette immersion.
Connect the recording chamber with the silver/silver chloride ground electrode by a 3 M KCl agar bridge.
Form a giga-ohm seal with the cardiomyocytes using a square 5 mV test pulse at a holding potential of 0 mV.
Compensate the pipette capacitance in cell-attached mode by adjusting the “Fast” and “Slow” knobs.
Rupture the membrane to achieve whole-cell configuration with a resistance of at least one giga-ohm.
Hold the membrane potential at 0 mV during continuous perfusion.
Perform whole-cell recordings at room temperature (21°C–22°C) using an Axopatch 200A amplifier and pClamp10 software.
Digitally filter the recordings at 1 kHz and digitize them at 2 kHz.
Perfuse the cells with a bath solution containing 10 mM salicylate for 3 minutes to isolate the NLC component from prestin function.
Record the salicylate-sensitive capacitive currents during perfusion.
Use pClamp 10, Microsoft Excel, Origin 6.1, and GraphPad Prism software to analyze the capacitive currents.
Determine total membrane capacitance (Cm) by analyzing the capacitive currents and measuring the input resistance (Rin) at each step voltage (Vc).
Calculate Cm using the formula Cm=(Rin/Rm)^2*Q/Vc, where Rin is the input resistance determined by the steady state current and Vc.
Determine Rm as membrane resistance, Rs as series resistance which can be calculated by the time constant (τ) of the capacitor discharge current, charge movement (Q), step voltage and Rin.
Determine the NLC.
Calculate Cm as Cln + Cv, where Cln is linear capacitance and Cv is nonlinear capacitance.
Express normalized NLC as [Cm - Cln] / Cln.
Fit Cv with the first derivative of a Boltzmann function describing nonlinear charge movement.
